title: Texture-stage DMA channel selector A vs B -- pbkit-aliased smoke (v0.1)
purpose: Allocate a 1x1 SZ_A8R8G8B8 texture (single RED pixel). Render a left and right half-screen quad. Left half binds the texture with FORMAT_CONTEXT_DMA = 0 (channel A); right half with = 2 (channel B per pgraph.c:2679-2680, which only promotes CONTEXT_DMA == 2 to internal dma_select=1; the natural field encoding 0/1/2/3 collapses to 0=A, 2=B). v0.1 is a SMOKE TEST UNDER PBKIT-DEFAULT ALIASING: nxdk's pbkit configures both SET_CONTEXT_DMA_A and SET_CONTEXT_DMA_B to point at the SAME RAMIN object (#3) which resolves to base 0 of VRAM. So this v0.1 cannot distinguish a routing regression that swaps dma_a and dma_b internally -- both channels alias the same VRAM. v0.1 IS useful as a non-zero-CONTEXT_DMA round-trip smoke (CONTEXT_DMA=2 doesn't crash the texture-bind path and produces correct RED output) and as a documentation oracle for the correct field encoding + the aliasing caveat. v0.1 is NOT a regression gate for per-channel base-address translation. v0.2 (tracked task #18) needs an xbed_dma helper that writes a custom DMA object to RAMIN at a distinct base, lets the XBE configure DMA B independently from A, and verifies both halves render identical content from their respective bases.
